items.title: Family members, military men among 32 killed in NAF plane crash in Ondo
items.description: ***25 passengers, 7 crew members on board — Minister By Dayo Johnson, Regional Editor, South-West, Kingsley Omonobi, Johnbosco Agbakwuru & Dickson Omobola AKURE — No fewer than 32 persons, including family members of military personnel and crew died yesterday as the ATR-42 plane they were travelling in crashed into a swamp opposite the Naval Base at Igbokoda, Ondo State. The aircraft, which crashed in the early hours of yesterday, had on board airmen, soldiers and their family members. Sources disclosed that some of the family members include children who were returning to school, and other family members who had visited their bread-winners serving in Edo and Delta states. According to sources, the turbo-prop aircraft was on a logistics mission to Lagos for NAF operations and afforded families, particularly of military personnel the opportunity to be flown to Lagos. It was learned yesterday that the difficulty in releasing the names of the dead passengers from military authorities stemmed from the fact that civilian passengers were onboard, with efforts ongoing to reach out to them first. While mourning victims of the crash, President Bola Tinubu, also yesterday ordered immediate investigation into the crash. He declared a three-day national mourning for the victims and directed that flags be flown at half-mast throughout the country as a mark of respect to the officers. LG chairman, police confirm incident, military gear recovered, fingers bad weather Confirming the crash in a telephone interview, the chairman of Ilaje Local Government Area, Mr. Maurice Oripelaye, said military gear had been recovered from the crash site. Speaking through his Chief Press Secretary, Taiwo Sadare, the LG chairman said: “Our findings showed that it was poor weather condition that affected the pilot. “He was trying to maneuver, but the poor weather condition affected the pilot. It crashed into a swampy area very close to the water, along the swampy area, at the back of Naval Base. Also, the state police spokesperson, DSP Jimoh Abayomi, who also confirmed the crash, said: “Details surrounding the incident are still emerging, as efforts to establish the full circumstances continue. “The command urges members of the public, particularly residents of Igbokoda and adjoining communities, to remain calm and refrain from circulating unverified information. The public will be duly informed as soon as further credible information becomes available.” NAF activates immediate search, rescue operation Reacting, the Nigerian Air Force, NAF, said it had activated an immediate Search and Rescue operation on the crash. NAF Director of Public Relations and Information, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, said in a statement: “The aircraft was on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos when the accident occurred. Search and Rescue operations, in coordination with relevant authorities and emergency response agencies, are currently ongoing. “NAF is committed to ensuring the success of the ongoing Search and Rescue efforts. Further details will be communicated in due course.” The NAF spokesperson did not, however, disclose the number of casualties. Keyamo confirms military aircraft crash However, Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, confirmed that 32 persons, including 25 passengers and seven crew members died in the crash. Keyamo said the aircraft, with tail number NGR 931, was en route Lagos from Benin when air traffic controllers lost contact with it at about 9:13am. The minister, who disclosed this on X, formerly Twitter, stated: “I regret to inform the general public that Air Traffic Controllers have informed me of the disappearance of a military aircraft with tail number NGR 931, enroute Lagos from Benin at 0913 hours earlier today. All efforts to raise the aircraft on radio proved abortive. “Subsequently information, however, confirmed that the military aircraft crashed close to the Naval Base at Igbokoda, Ondo State. The wreckage has been located and search and rescue operations are ongoing. “Preliminary information suggests that there were 25 passengers and seven crew members on board. While the control and regulation of military aircraft are completely outside the authority of the Ministry of Aviation, and Civil Aviation Authority, I have just spoken to the Chief of Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, and pledged our total cooperation and assistance in the search and rescue efforts ongoing.” Aiyedatiwa mourns In a swift response, Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa expressed heartfelt sympathy to the Chief of Air Staff, the entire NAF family, and the families of all personnel and passengers on board the ill-fated aircraft. In a statement by his Chief Press Secretary, Ebenezer Adeniyan, the governor said: “Our thoughts and prayers are with them at this difficult time.” Adeniyan said the governor had directed the State Emergency Management Agency, SEMA, the Ministry of Health and relevant security agencies to immediately mobilise and offer full logistical and human support to NAF and other emergency agencies in the ongoing rescue operations. The statement read: “The governor of Ondo State, Lucky Orimisan Aiyedatiwa, has received with deep sadness the news of the crash of a Nigerian Air Force aircraft in Igbokoda, headquarters of Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State, in the early hours of today, Monday, October 5, 2026. “According to preliminary reports confirmed by the Nigerian Air Force Director of Public Relations and Information, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, the aircraft, an ATR-42 with tail number NGR 931, was on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos when it crashed in a swampy area opposite the Naval Base in Igbokoda. “The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr. Festus Keyamo, has confirmed that 25 passengers and seven crew members were on board. “On behalf of the government and good people of Ondo State, Governor Aiyedatiwa expresses his heartfelt sympathy to the Chief of Air Staff, the entire Nigerian Air Force family, and the families of all personnel and passengers on board the ill-fated aircraft. “The governor has been in contact with the leadership of the Nigerian Air Force, the Ilaje Local Government Chairman, Maurice Oripelaye, and security agencies on ground. “To aid ongoing efforts, Governor Aiyedatiwa has directed the State Emergency Management Agency, SEMA, the Ministry of Health, and relevant security agencies to immediately mobilise and offer full logistical and human support to the Nigerian Air Force and other emergency response agencies in the search and rescue operations currently ongoing at the crash site. “The governor has also directed that the area be cordoned off and secured to allow for smooth and unhindered rescue operations, while urging residents of Igbokoda and adjoining communities to remain calm, cooperate with emergency responders, and refrain from spreading unverified information.” Panic in coastal community as residents recount loud sound Meanwhile, a resident, who said many occupants of the aircraft might have died, said: “It happened this morning (yesterday). We heard a very loud sound from the area where the incident occurred, but we couldn’t get there because the place is a swampy area inside the creek. We were just looking at it from afar. “The accident caused panic as both the young and old people in the community fled in different directions. “But the police and the military later came around for rescue, but the occupants may have died there,” he said. Another resident, Oluboyo Olusola, said “after the accident, I was here personally. I saw many things. I saw parts of the aircraft, I saw body parts that were scattered and clothes. That means everybody inside that aircraft are dead.” Monarch fears no survivor, says aircraft submerged in swamps Also speaking, the traditional ruler of the community, the Olu of Igbokoda, Oba Afolabi Odidiomo, said he initially feared it was a commercial aircraft because of the potential number of casualties. Oba Odidiomo said: “I was in court when the incident happened, and I directed some of my palace officials to visit the site. “At that time, nobody could determine whether it was an airplane or a helicopter. I was worried because it must not be a plane, because the number of casualties would be just too high. Our first thanks to Almighty God is that it did not happen inside the town; otherwise, the casualties would have been too many. “The aircraft crashed into the river and a swampy area. It was raining when the accident happened and the place was waterlogged. “The aircraft did not catch fire, but a substantial part of it has gone into the water. We cannot describe the exact situation for now, but from my investigation and what we have gathered so far, there was no survivor.” Tinubu mourns NAF personnel in Ondo jet crash, orders thorough investigation In his immediate reaction to the crash, President Bola Tinubu expressed profound sadness over the accident A statement by the presidential spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, said the aircraft was on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos when the accident occurred. The President extended his deepest condolences to the family of the 25 passengers and seven crew members involved, the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, and all officers, airmen and airwomen of the Nigerian Air Force. “This is a painful moment for our Armed Forces and for the entire nation. Our Air Force personnel put their lives on the line every day to secure Nigeria. Their sacrifice will never be forgotten. “The Chief of Air Staff has briefed me, and I have directed the Nigerian Air Force to immediately commence a thorough investigation into the cause of the crash to prevent future occurrences. “I commend the Nigerian Air Force for activating an immediate Search and Rescue operation, following the accident.. “I pray for the repose of the souls of the gallant officers and for Almighty God to grant their families and the Nigerian Air Force the fortitude to bear the unfortunate loss. “I assure the Nigerian Air Force of the continued support of our administration as they continue their vital role in securing our nation. “I also commend the swift response of first responders and the Ondo State government at the crash site,” Tinubu said. The post Family members, military men among 32 killed in NAF plane crash in Ondo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Farming reform
items.description: THE Kissan Board Pakistan has demanded that agriculture receive at least 10pc of the federal and provincial budgets to lower input costs and address recurring deficits. The farmers’ body also wants support prices of Rs5,000 per 40kg for wheat and Rs700 for sugarcane, citing declining profitability. It has criticised urea shortages, high electricity bills, weak fruit sector returns, and the Pak-Afghan border closure, warning of protests if their demands are not met. Their case for enhanced budgetary allocations deserves consideration. The sector contributes about 22pc of GDP and supports nearly 60pc of the population, but receives only 2-3pc of allocations. However, money alone will not fix matters. Nor should a larger allocation become another excuse for inefficient price subsidies. Pakistan has spent decades trying to support farmers through administered prices, input subsidies and other interventions. This has distorted markets, encouraged inefficient production and benefited better-connected producers more than small farmers. Public investment should, instead, address structural weaknesses that depress farm productivity. Water management, irrigation efficiency, farm-to-market roads, storage, research, extension services and better seed technology need sustained investment. Mechanisation must become a central priority. Shared machinery services, and affordable financing can help spread mechanisation without imposing a massive capital burden on farmers. The aim should be to lower production costs, while raising yields and quality. That requires modernisation, not perpetual protection from market forces. Farmers cannot become globally competitive if they face unpredictable trade policies, distorted input markets, poor access to finance, unreliable power and water supply, and arbitrary official intervention in crop markets. Policy must encourage farmers to respond to prices and market demand rather than to official announcements. Pakistan also needs to look beyond the farm gate. A stronger downstream processing industry can reduce post-harvest losses, add value to farm output and create export opportunities. Better cold storage, grading, packaging, processing, and logistics are essential, and can help stabilise markets when production falls by allowing stocks to be preserved. This matters because agriculture is treated as a production problem when it is really a value-chain issue. Producing more wheat, fruit, vegetables, sugarcane or rice means little if large quantities are wasted, farmers receive poor returns, and consumers face shortages or sudden price spikes. Farmers, therefore, are right to demand greater public investment. But the test should not be the size of the allocation. It should be where the money goes and what it achieves. Agriculture needs investment, but not another round of costly interventions. It needs infrastructure, technology, mechanisation, processing, markets, and policies that make farming competitive rather than dependent on the state’s largesse. Published in Dawn, October 6th, 2026

items.title: Cameroun: il y a dix ans, la mobilisation des avocats qui précédait l’embrasement des régions anglophones
items.description: Au Cameroun, c'était il y a bientôt dix ans. En octobre, puis novembre 2016, la mobilisation des avocats, enseignants et étudiants des régions anglophones prend de l'ampleur. La répression des forces de l'ordre ravive alors des velléités de retour au fédéralisme et de sécessionnisme. S'ensuivent, début 2017, des journées villes mortes, des boycotts, des incidents de plus en plus violents, jusqu'à déboucher sur un conflit armé entre groupes séparatistes et forces gouvernementales.

items.title: Éthiopie: reconduit sur fond de tensions, le Premier ministre Abiy Ahmed défend un accès à la mer
items.description: Quatre mois après les élections législatives du 1ᵉʳ juin, Abiy Ahmed a été réinvesti lundi 5 octobre Premier ministre par les députés du Parlement éthiopien. Seul candidat, le dirigeant entame un nouveau mandat de cinq ans à la tête du pays, alors que la guerre a repris depuis le 23 septembre. Dans son discours devant les nouveaux élus, il a une nouvelle fois défendu la nécessité pour l’Éthiopie de disposer d’un accès à la mer, alors qu’une éventuelle implication de l’Érythrée dans les affrontements de ces derniers jours fait craindre un conflit régional.

items.title: Defence Minister expresses deep sorrow over crash of NAF aircraft
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa Rtd, has expressed deep sorrow over the tragic crash of NAF ATR 42 aircraft and the loss of officers and airmen who were involved in a routine flight mission to Lagos, describing them as personnel who exemplified the highest standards of loyalty and commitment to the defence of the country. In a statement he personally signed, Gen Musa offered condolences to President Bola Tinubu, the leadership of the Armed Forces, and most especially, the immediate families, loved ones, and colleagues of our fallen heroes. He said, “It is with a profound sense of grief and heavy heart that I, on behalf of the Ministry of Defence and the entire Armed Forces of Nigeria, express deep sorrow over the tragic crash of our military aircraft with tail number NAF 931 involving dedicated personnel of the Armed Forces. “This painful incident claimed the lives of brave officers and airmen who were engaged in routine flight mission while serving our nation with courage, unyielding devotion, and selfless patriotism. “The loss of these valiant patriots is an irreparable blow not only to the military high command and their comrades-in-arms, but to the entire Federal Republic of Nigeria. “These fine officers and men exemplify the highest standards of military professionalism, loyalty, and commitment to the defence of our Fatherland. “On behalf of the Ministry of Defence, I extend our heartfelt condolences to the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, the leadership of the Armed Forces, and most especially, the immediate families, loved ones, and colleagues of our fallen heroes. “We share in your immense grief and stand shoulder-to-shoulder with you during this tragic hour. “Our hearts also go out to the families of the civilians on board the ill-fated aircraft, we share your grief. “A comprehensive investigation into the circumstances surrounding this unfortunate crash has been ordered to ascertain the cause and ensure all necessary operational safety protocols are reinforced across our military aviation units. “We pray that the Almighty God grants the souls of the departed eternal repose, and give their families, the military community, and all Nigerians the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss.” The post Defence Minister expresses deep sorrow over crash of NAF aircraft appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘Bamba’s message was clever, very clever’ – Akomea on NPP election upset
items.description: Newly elected NPP Third Vice Chairperson Nana Akomea has described Kojo Bamba’s campaign message as “clever” after the latter defied expectations in the party’s national executive election. Nana Akomea finished third in the race, an outcome he says surprised him after he had expected to place first or second. “I was expected to be first or second, not third.” He admitted that the result was disappointing, although he had anticipated a difficult contest. “Yes, it disappointed me a little, but I knew it was going to be tough.” Nana Akomea said the race was extremely close, with only small margins separating the leading candidates. “And when you look at maybe the top four, it’s very close.” He said the narrow margins showed how competitive the contest was. “The top four: 2900 and something, 2900 and something, 2900 and something, 3000 and something, 3000. It’s very close, very tight.” But Nana Akomea believes Kojo Bamba’s campaign strategy helped him outperform expectations. He said Bamba was not given much of a chance by the polls but delivered a message that differed from that of the other leading candidates. “Now, why I thought it was going to be difficult was that Bamba, whom nobody gave much chance, and the poll that you referred to about him, I think gave him 5% or 6% or something.” “But you know, Bamba’s message was clever, very clever. His message was different.” According to Nana Akomea, several of the leading candidates largely campaigned on their experience and long service to the party. “Whilst Nana B., myself, Mustapha Hamid, Ahiagbah, and all those people, we had basically the same message that we had served the party faithfully for a long time.” He said the candidates also relied on their established profiles within the NPP. “We’ve had a lot of experience, and we had a profile, a brand in the party, and want to use that brand to help the party.” Bamba, however, adopted a different approach by focusing his campaign on protecting delegates and the integrity of the election. “Bamba’s message was that these people—they’ve served the party for a long time. I don’t intend to compete with them; what I want to give you is your security. security.” Nana Akomea said the message allowed Bamba to present himself differently from the other candidates. “So you vote for two of them. Two of them, and then make sure that you admin for the sake of your security.” “So they will do the work, and I’ll just protect the ballot and protect you.” Nana Akomea also said he paid little attention to opinion polls before the election because candidates had direct access to delegates. He said candidates could assess reactions to their messages by meeting delegates face-to-face. “Don’t let T-shirts come between you and them. Don’t let them focus on caps and T-shirts and paraphernalia.” “And you don’t need the polls because you are meeting the people directly, and you can know from their reaction if your message resonates with them.”

Rodeada de activistas del Sindicato de Inquilinas, de caras conocidas y muy identificadas con el progresismo —como Ana Belén, Juan Diego Botto y Carlos Bardem—, Maricarmen Abascal, de 87 años, abandonaba su casa en camilla, desahuciada por el fondo que la compró, después de 70 años pagando su alquiler. items.title: Todos los proyectos que caen con las nuevas elecciones tras una legislatura con 22 leyes y 43 decretos
items.description: El 29 de noviembre de 2023, hace tres años, el Rey inauguró esta XV legislatura , marcada desde el inicio por la precariedad parlamentaria, pero en la que se han abordado y debatido hasta 158 iniciativas de todo tipo, las más relevantes a través de la figura en teoría excepcional del real decreto ley. Se han aprobado 43, pero muchas normas trascendentes han vuelto a quedar en el tintero: la modernización de la justicia, la regulación de los lobbies , el estatuto del becario, la bajada de ratio en las aulas, el veto de las redes a los menores de 16 años, la ley de cine o el Fondo de Liquidez Autonómico (FLA) aprobado por el Consejo de Ministros en 2025, entre otros. El Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez, que anticipará ahora las nuevas elecciones para el 29 de noviembre de 2026, quiere que el último gran debate en el Congreso recupere y convalide los decretos sobre vivienda que decayeron el viernes pasado en un pleno extraordinario, pero algo retocados para salvar problemas legales y por medio de una especial Diputación Permanente, un órgano previsto para cubrir los periodos inhábiles normales de la Cámara . El Ejecutivo y sus socios habituales sí dispondrían ahí de mayoría por la mínima si no falla el PNV. Seguir leyendo Sin margen para los Presupuestos La disolución de las Cortes hace imposible que el Gobierno que salga de las urnas apruebe unos nuevos Presupuestos en tiempo y forma, de modo que, pase lo que pase tras la cita electoral, España empezará el año 2027 con las cuentas de 2023 otra vez prorrogadas, en esta ocasión por cuarto año consecutivo. Crédito al consumo Queda en el aire la ley de crédito al consumo, que limita de forma transitoria al 22% la TAE de este tipo de préstamos y de las tarjetas 'revolving'. Nueva ley antiblanqueo También quedará en suspenso la ley antiblanqueo, que se proponía exigir a las plataformas de criptoactivos revelar a las autoridades cada apertura y cierre. Estatuto del becario El Ministerio de Trabajo también tiene varios proyectos legislativos en marcha que decaerán. El que más tiempo lleva bloqueado en el Parlamento es el estatuto del becario, una norma que buscaba atenuar la precariedad que sufren los estudiantes en prácticas. 21.000 millones Una medida económica especialmente ambiciosa que decae es la reforma del sistema de financiación autonómica, que lleva 12 años pendiente. Hacienda presentó en enero una propuesta para cambiar el modelo y dotarlo con 21.000 millones adicionales. Condonación de deuda También decae la iniciativa para condonar 83.000 millones de deuda autonómica, pese a encontrarse en una etapa legislativa algo más avanzada que la reforma de la financiación autonómica. Recaudación de IRPF Este era el siguiente paso en la negociación después del modelo de financiación, aunque era muy poco probable que se cerrase durante esta legislatura. PSC y ERC habían pactado que la Agencia Tributaria de Cataluña empezaría a recaudar el 100% del IRPF a partir de 2026. Rodalies El acuerdo para el traspaso de Rodalies apenas ha empezado a desplegarse este año. La empresa mixta con el Estado empezó a operar el 1 de enero, pero esta debía dar su primer salto con el traspaso de la R1, que une L’Hospitalet de Llobregat con Blanes y Maçanet-Massanes. Ratios en las aulas Una de las medidas centrales del Ejecutivo para mejorar la situación del profesorado era la bajada de las ratios, que el Gobierno llevó como proyecto de ley al Congreso hace un año, y con la que quería reducir de 30 a 25 el número máximo de alumnos por clase en la ESO, y de 25 a 22 en Primaria. Ley de violencia vicaria machista En materia de igualdad la norma más avanzada es la ley de violencia vicaria machista, “una de las formas más crueles y devastadoras de violencia de género”, según la definió del último texto conocido. Ley de Familias Fue aprobada la legislatura pasada y este Gobierno de coalición volvió a enviarla al Parlamento hace ya más de dos años. Y allí ha estado todo este tiempo, bloqueada, debido a la falta de apoyos. Ley de Pacientes Es la norma que este ministerio tenía más esperanzas en aprobar por su consenso en un Congreso muy fragmentado. La legislación pretendía dar reconocimiento jurídico específico a las asociaciones de pacientes para garantizar su participación estable en órganos de gobernanza sanitaria. Ley del Cine Hace apenas unos días por fin había arrancado su ponencia en la Comisión de Cultura del Congreso, cuyo visto bueno se antojaba necesario antes de la votación final en el pleno. A posteriori, llegó tarde: hasta 70 veces se fue ampliando el plazo de presentación de enmiendas del texto, mientras los meses y los años pasaban. Oficina Española de Derechos de Autor Era 2022 cuando el anterior ministro de Cultura, el socialista Miquel Iceta, la anunció. Calificó la propiedad intelectual como “un pilar fundamental de las industrias culturales”, recordó que aporta un 3,4% del PIB y aseguró que la normativa debía reforzar y agilizar la actividad administrativa que corresponde al Estado en ese ámbito. Inteligencia Artificial generativa en el trabajo cultural El tercer intento del Gobierno en este ámbito no ha durado ni un mes. Primero, Cultura impulsó un real decreto, que retiró ante el rechazo de buena parte del sector. Luego lo intentó Trabajo, por la misma vía, pero el Consejo de Estado opinó que cambios de tal calado afectaban a derechos fundamentales y hacía falta una ley. De ahí al anteproyecto y, ahora, una vez más a la casilla de salida. Tauromaquia Otra iniciativa que surgió hace unas semanas, aunque viene de mucho más lejos. En febrero de 2025, miles de voluntarios entregaron al Congreso el resultado de meses de trabajo: 664.777 firmas de apoyo a una Iniciativa Legislativa Popular (ILP) que planteaba al Parlamento quitarle a la tauromaquia la categoría de patrimonio cultural y, por tanto, la protección a nivel estatal.

items.title: El PSOE encara las elecciones entre la ilusión y el alivio: “Nos vamos a reivindicar con orgullo”
items.description: El PSOE encara el adelanto electoral con alivio y el ánimo recobrado pero sin hacerse trampas al solitario. Los socialistas son conscientes de que el 29 de noviembre se jugarán el Gobierno en unas circunstancias muy difíciles y tras sufrir un desgaste muy importante por los escándalos de corrupción y la reacción tardía a la crisis de Ceuta. Aun así todos sus dirigentes coinciden, en público y en privado, en que la convocatoria les llega en el mejor momento posible. “Dentro de lo que hay, que es muchísimo mejor de lo que había hace tan solo dos semanas, cuando todo era Ceuta y nada más que Ceuta”, resume un líder territorial. “El incentivo para convocar era total: las movilizaciones en la calle, la izquierda reactivada y Ceuta enterrado en la vivienda”, apunta el responsable de una federación mediana. items.title: Feijóo no teme otra remontada de Sánchez y niega el paralelismo con las elecciones de 2023
items.description: Alberto Núñez Feijóo vive uno de los momentos de mayor confianza de su carrera. Convencido de que ha llegado su gran oportunidad, el líder del PP lo verbalizó este lunes ante el congreso de la empresa familiar: “Estoy en el momento más importante de mi vida política. Sé que hay muchos que me están mirando”. Horas antes, en la sede de Génova, 13, se habían vivido escenas de euforia tras el anuncio de Pedro Sánchez de adelantar las elecciones al próximo 29 de noviembre. El comité de dirección rompió en aplausos poco antes de que el líder bajara a la sala de prensa para pronunciar su primer discurso tras el anticipo electoral que los populares llevaban mucho tiempo reclamando. Entre sus colaboradores más próximos predominaba la sensación de que el escenario, al fin, juega a su favor. Aunque nadie da la victoria por descontada y el líder popular se dispone a recorrer el país de arriba abajo en las próximas semanas, en el PP se descarta cualquier paralelismo con las generales de 2023, cuando Pedro Sánchez logró frustrar todos los pronósticos, y se abre paso la convicción de que, esta vez sí, Feijóo está a las puertas de alcanzar el poder. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Jeanne, la nieta que se nacionalizó “por la memoria” de su abuelo exiliado y que no sabe si podrá votar el 29 de noviembre
items.description: Lo único que Jeanne Robles sabía de los orígenes de su abuelo, José Robles, era lo que él le contaba cuando era pequeña. Una historia que, durante años, a ella le pareció casi rocambolesca. José, nacido en Málaga, había subido a un tren con apenas siete años que se dirigía a Valence, una ciudad del sureste de Francia, donde una familia francesa lo acogió y lo adoptó en el mismo andén. De niña, Jeanne no lograba entenderlo. “¿Por qué un niño tan pequeño se subiría a un tren para irse tan lejos de su familia?”, se preguntaba. Ya de adulta, decidió investigar. Durante años recorrió archivos en España y Francia hasta reconstruir la otra vida de su abuelo, la que había quedado atrás cuando tuvo que exiliarse en enero de 1937, apenas un mes antes de que las tropas franquistas tomaran Málaga. Seguir leyendo

items.title: ¿Qué dirán las encuestas electorales dentro de unos días?
Toma de conciencia
items.description: Con las dos últimas generaciones de jóvenes se ha llevado a cabo un experimento de tecnología social que ha salido mal. Sólo les ha salido bien a los tecnocaciques que capitanearon esa demolición de todos los valores necesarios para la convivencia pacífica. Sin embargo, a raíz del episodio de desahucio de su casa de una anciana de 87 años en Madrid, ha habido una toma de conciencia colectiva entre muchos jóvenes que anula esa sensación de que la ideología individualista y reaccionaria podía haberlos seducido. Aún no hemos llegado a ver una manifestación contra la dominación tecnológica, una huelga general de desconexión, un revivir de ese raro placer que les produjo el día del apagón, pero quizá la lleguemos a ver algún día. Cuando los jóvenes reclaman el derecho a encontrar un hogar digno lo que están haciendo es gritar que no se consuelan con ese espacio virtual donde se les entretiene, distrae y ordeña sin que obtengan apenas ningún beneficio palpable. Cautivos de un encantamiento sin arraigo en la realidad, las grandes manifestaciones en reclamo de una ley de vivienda pueden representar su despertar. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El fantasma del pucherazo vuelve a pasearse por el PP y Vox
Sánchez y el placer del error ajeno
items.description: “¿Qué te apuestas?”. La pregunta es siempre el paso último, la demostración final de que la persona cree firmemente en lo que dice. A veces es un reto, otras un juego, en ocasiones un desacuerdo, casi siempre una provocación… En otros muchos casos, se trata de una predicción. Cuando se da entre amigos, se juega una cena, 10 euros… O cualquier otra cosa que ninguna de las dos partes acostumbra a cobrarse, aunque está bien no olvidar nunca quién ganó. Para que el perdedor respete un poco y aprenda. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Norman Foster: “En vivienda se ha desplazado todo de lo público a lo privado, hay que encontrar un mejor equilibrio”
items.description: Su traje de terciopelo color berenjena, camisa negra y corbata lila con lunares blancos destacan entre los tonos más sobrios de las autoridades y las paredes blancas de su nueva criatura. Decir que tiene un aspecto formidable a sus 91 años es quedarse muy corto. Norman Foster, el arquitecto vivo más importante del mundo, pasea ligero por las salas del Museo de Bellas Artes de Bilbao, recién concluida su renovación a cargo del mancuniano y que este martes abre sus puertas al público. Asiste al destapamiento de una fantástica escultura de Kiefer en el jardín de la entrada y después, cuatro pisos más arriba, muestra dos de Anthony Caro en la nueva terraza. Las tres piezas han sido cedidas por Norman y Elena Foster al museo, que desde arriba ofrece una vista privilegiada a esta ciudad a cuya transformación contribuyó Foster hace más de 30 años, cuando diseñó el metro de Bilbao. Tras un paseo que se le ha hecho corto —“Éramos un grupo muy numeroso y no pudimos verlo todo”, lamenta— comparece sonriente ante los medios y autoridades y, después, aún ha reservado tiempo, antes de la multitudinaria cena en el atrio del museo, para una entrevista con EL PAÍS. La conversación con una de las personas que, durante seis décadas, más ha reflexionado e innovado en torno a las ciudades se produce mientras dos de los principales desafíos a los que estas se enfrentan se hacen palpables en la calle: las consecuencias del cambio climático, en forma de violentas tormentas que han causado inundaciones la víspera en esta misma ciudad, y el malestar de toda una generación por la imposibilidad de acceder a la vivienda, que se ha cristalizado en acampadas y protestas por todo el país. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La aldea gala de la crisis de la vivienda: Marinaleda, con alquileres entre cero y 24 euros mensuales
items.description: La grave crisis de la vivienda también tiene su aldea gala: Marinaleda , al Este de la provincia de Sevilla, acumula 300 casas públicas del total de 1.000 que hay en este pueblo jornalero en pleno olivar, casi una de cada tres. Sus inquilinos pagan entre cero y 24 euros de alquiler mensual al Ayuntamiento, que lleva 40 años construyendo viviendas cuya propiedad nunca ha traspasado a los moradores. Esa cuota irrisoria que pagan las familias levanta incredulidad, pero también admiración. ¿Cómo ha podido levantar Marinaleda ese enorme parque público? ¿Cuál es su secreto? ¿Es su modelo exportable a otros pueblos o ciudades? Seguir leyendo

items.title: Sarah Schulman, escritora: “Los agresores se presentan ahora a sí mismos como víctimas”
items.description: El victimismo, su explotación y también su uso político para justificar la cruelad, ha sido uno de los temas que más ha investigado Sarah Schulman (Nueva York, 68 años). Han pasado 10 años desde que la escritora, activista LGTBIQ+ y también historiadora del sida, publicase El conflicto no es abuso , que ahora edita en español Capitán Swing. “Tristemente, resulta que el libro fue profético”, explica la autora por videoconferencia, “se publicó antes de que Trump fuera elegido, y él, en cierto modo, ha demostrado que todas las tesis expuestas eran ciertas: toda su retórica gira en torno a que él es una víctima. También lo vemos en Netanyahu . Esa idea de que el perpetrador, el agresor, se presenta a sí mismo como víctima es, por desgracia, la norma a nivel global”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Un mes con Silvio Rodríguez en España: “El mundo parece estar sumiéndose en una edad oscura”
items.description: Silvio Rodríguez se levanta de la silla y deja a un lado la guitarra. Es la única vez en un concierto que dura dos horas que va a interpretar una canción de pie. Los músicos se marchan. Solo se queda en el escenario la familia: su pareja, la flautista Niurka González, y la hija de ambos, Malva, de 23 años, acompañando a las voces y al piano. Una reunión íntima, casi como si coincidieran en la cocina de su casa. La canción que interpretan no la firma el cubano. “Enemigo de la guerra y su reverso la medalla”, entona Silvio con esa voz inconfundible y aún vigorosa a sus 79 años. El público estalla en una ovación. Muchos no pueden contener las lágrimas; otro espectador grita: “¡Viva la revolución!”. La belleza, esa canción que compuso Luis Eduardo Aute contraponiendo la armonía humana a la barbarie, embaucó a un repleto Movistar Arena, en Madrid, el pasado domingo en el último de los 10 conciertos que el legendario músico ofreció en España. Seguir leyendo

La cuestión puede parecer menor hasta que “va cobrando cada vez más resonancia cuanto más piensas en ello”, escribe Vanessa Friedman en The New York Times en un artículo titulado ¿Son los botones sexistas?. items.title: Sexto día de temporal: los chubascos y tormentas se generalizan, con los más intensos en el centro y el tercio norte
items.description: La inestabilidad atmosférica aumentará este martes en España, cuando se cumplen seis días de inicio del intenso temporal , y los chubascos con tormentas se generalizan. ”Podrán caer casi en cualquier parte, aunque con mayor intensidad en zonas del tercio norte y del centro del área peninsular", indica el portavoz de la Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (Aemet), Rubén del Campo. Estas precipitaciones “podrán ser fuertes e incluso muy fuertes con acumulados importantes en zonas de Extremadura, oeste de Castilla-La Mancha y el entorno del Sistema Central”. Además, podrán ir acompañados de granizo. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Las afectadas por los problemas de suministro de hormonas para la menopausia: “Esto no es un capricho, es una necesidad vital”
items.description: Una de ellas se siente una “yonqui” cada vez que va a la farmacia a pedir su tratamiento. Otra cruzó la frontera con Portugal y volvió con seis botes de un tratamiento que necesita para cuidar de sus huesos y que en España no está ni se le espera . Una tercera ha reunido más de 25.000 firmas desde su casa de Cuenca, que presenta hoy ante el Ministerio de Sanidad , y la cuarta ayudó a montar un mapa de farmacias con existencias que, a principios del verano, solo marcaba dos. Rebeca, Silvia, Marta e Inanna tienen edades, ciudades y motivos distintos para seguir una terapia hormonal : los síntomas de la menopausia, una osteoporosis prematura, la necesidad de volver a dormir y trabajar, una transición de género. Las une el mismo medicamento, Lenzetto, en falta desde marzo, y la misma búsqueda de alternativas que también han ido desapareciendo de las farmacias . Seguir leyendo

items.title: El desalojo de la playa de El Trampolín dispara los “retornos voluntarios” en Ceuta: 900 regresos en un día
items.description: El domingo, primer día del desalojo de El Trampolín , se disparó el número de migrantes que regresan “voluntariamente” a Marruecos. La proporción fue inédita: de las 1.100 personas sacadas de la playa en autobuses custodiados por la Policía Nacional, retornaron al país vecino unas 900, hasta un 80% del total, según datos del Ejecutivo. Apenas dos centenares optaron por quedarse en el centro de registro de datos de El Tarajal para su posterior. La operación continuó este lunes con el desmantelamiento total del poblado. Pero, cuando los agentes retomaron el operativo a primera hora de la mañana, buena parte de los migrantes habían escapado a las montañas para evitar su traslado forzoso al paso fronterizo. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Así son las imágenes de los “retornos voluntarios” de migrantes en Ceuta tras el desalojo de El Trampolín
items.description: El desalojo del asentamiento de migrantes de la playa de El Trampolín ha desembocado en 1.100 retornos “voluntarios” en dos días. El primero, efectuado el domingo, volvieron 900 personas de las 1.100 que había en las tiendas precarias. El segundo, este lunes, 200 de unas 300. En el vídeo que acompaña la noticia se explica ese proceso y se pueden ver las imágenes de los regresos .

items.description: El lunes amanece en Copacabana como cualquier otro. items.title: Karlos Arguiñano pela una yuca en su programa y las redes sociales de Latinoamérica se encienden
items.description: “Se pela superfácil con el pelador de siempre, el de las patatas”. Así comenzaba Karlos Arguiñano a pelar una yuca hace solo unos días en su programa de televisión. Se disponía a hacer unos chips de guarnición para una dorada a la lima . Hasta aquí, todo normal. Sin embargo, cuando este momento del programa llegó en forma de clip a las redes sociales del cocinero, se desató la polémica. “Más de un Latinoamericano sufriendo un infarto al verlo”; “Qué ley permite denunciar este crimen? Vulneración a los derechos de la yuca!!!”; o “Así es como se siente un italiano cuando parten por la mitad los espaguetis” son solo algunos de los miles de comentarios que hay en la publicación en los distintos perfiles de Arguiñano: más de 18.000 en Instagram, más de 5.000 en TikTok y unos 3.000 en Facebook, en su mayoría, de personas de países latinoamericanos donde la yuca se consume de forma habitual. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Here’s the latest.
Nana Akomea reveals why he was disappointed after placing third in NPP election
items.description: Newly elected NPP Third Vice Chairperson Nana Akomea has admitted he was disappointed after finishing third in the party’s national executive elections. Nana Akomea said he had expected to finish either first or second in the contest. “I was expected to be first or second, not third.” Speaking on Monday, he said the result disappointed him, although he knew the contest would be difficult. “Yes, it disappointed me a little, but I knew it was going to be tough.” He said the final results showed how closely contested the race was, with small differences separating the leading candidates. “And when you look at maybe the top four, it’s very close.” “The gap between myself and Mustafa was just about maybe 80, and then between myself and Nana B was just another 70 or so, and between Nana B and Kojo Bamba was maybe another 100 and something.” He said the closeness of the results made it difficult to draw a clear line between the leading candidates. “The top four: 2900 and something, 2900 and something, 2900 and something, 3000 and something. It’s very close, very tight.” Nana Akomea said he had paid little attention to opinion polls ahead of the election because he believed direct engagement with delegates was more important. “This one, you are meeting the delegates directly.” He said candidates had the opportunity to meet delegates face-to-face and assess their reactions to their messages. “Don’t let T-shirts come between you and them. Don’t let them focus on caps and T-shirts and paraphernalia, and you don’t need the polls because you are meeting the people directly.” Nana Akomea also attributed Kojo Bamba’s strong performance to a different campaign message. He said Bamba’s message stood apart from that of the other leading candidates. “But you know, Bamba’s message was clever, very clever. His message was different.” According to Nana Akomea, several of the leading candidates presented similar arguments based on their experience and long service to the NPP. “Whilst Nana B. myself, Mustapha Hamid, Ahiagbah, and all those people, we had basically the same message that we had served the party faithfully for a long time.” “We’ve had a lot of experience, and we had a profile, a brand in the party, and want to use that brand to help the party.” He said Bamba instead presented himself as someone who would focus on protecting delegates and the electoral process. “Bamba’s message was that these people-they’ve served the party for a long time. I don’t intend to compete with them, but what I want to give to you is your security.” “So you vote for two of them. Two of them, and then make sure that you admin for the sake of your security. So they will do the work, and I’ll just protect the ballot and protect you.”

items.title: Ondo plane crash: No survivors yet, only wreckage, IDs – Gov Aiyedatiwa
items.description: By Cynthia Alo Ondo State Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa has said no survivor has been recovered from Monday’s military aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ilaje Local Government Area of the state, with only wreckage of wings, identity cards and uniforms seen. Aiyedatiwa said rescue teams are yet to access the main body of the aircraft because it went deep into the swamp. The governor disclosed this on Monday night during an interview on Politics Today, a Channels Television programme. He said the aircraft, with 32 persons on board, 25 passengers and seven crew members, was a surveillance aircraft on its way from Benin to Lagos, which lost radio signal at about 9:15 a.m. He said information got to him at about 10:30 a.m. from the chairman of Ilaje Local Government that residents heard a sound like an air tremor before the aircraft dived into a swamp directly facing the Naval Forward Operating Base in Igbokoda. “They saw the wreckage from the wings, some ID cards and uniforms indicating it was a military aircraft. The main body went deep into the swamp area. They haven’t been able to search the aircraft itself yet,” he said. He said naval personnel, local emergency officials, Amotekun and residents moved into the creek with boats immediately the crash occurred, but no living soul was found. He said the site has been cordoned off, while hospitals in Igbokoda and Okitipupa have been placed on standby with ambulances recently procured for the 18 local governments. The governor said the Nigerian Air Force and the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau are investigating and will need to recover the black box to determine the exact cause. Speaking on the recent elimination of Abdussamad Ohida, a top ISWAP coordinator in Ondo forest, Aiyedatiwa said the clearance operation took place about five days ago after months of top secret surveillance. He said it was a joint operation involving the DSS, Nigerian Army, British intelligence officers and Amotekun, with no casualties recorded on the side of security forces. The governor explained that the coordinator took over after his former superior, a Central Nigeria ISWAP leader, was arrested by the DSS in 2023, adding that intelligence was generated from that arrest and from tracking of another leader earlier eliminated by DSS. He revealed that the criminals carry sophisticated weapons beyond AK-47, including GPMG, and had retaliated when security first launched attack. “When we launched the first attack, they retaliated. So we had to move back, heavily arm, do serious intelligence and mapping before we re-launched,” he said. Aiyedatiwa said the role of the UK was provision of intelligence and precision targeting equipment that Amotekun does not have, while Amotekun provided knowledge of terrain because many of its operatives are recruited local hunters. He said Ondo’s vast forests sharing boundaries with Kogi, Edo, Ekiti and Oyo have become a corridor for criminals fleeing military operations in Kogi and Kwara axis. According to him, what started as farmer-herder clashes years ago has graduated to terrorism, linking the group to the 2025 December 31 attack on Ipele police station and the 2022 Owo massacre. On whether the group plans to disrupt 2027 elections, he said their agenda in totality is to kill, destroy and disrupt in any form. The post Ondo plane crash: No survivors yet, only wreckage, IDs – Gov Aiyedatiwa appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Saudi Arabia urged to spare man sentenced to death over Facebook post
items.description: “I plead for mercy for the wrongs committed by my son. Please forgive him and send him back to us.” Speaking through tears, Rasamanickam Yogalakshmi made a desperate plea for the life of her eldest son, Anojan Sivarasa. The 24-year-old migrant worker is facing the death penalty in Saudi Arabia after an appellate court found him guilty of blasphemy against Islam and the Prophet Muhammad over a comment he made on Facebook. The case has sent shockwaves through Sri Lanka, sparking widespread concern and civil society petitions across the country. Multiple political parties and government bodies have co-ordinated diplomatic efforts seeking clemency. However, the family has had no updates on his condition since 28 September. The Sri Lankan government has instructed the family to refrain from making further statements while diplomatic efforts take place. Saudi authorities have not published an official execution timeline, and it remains unclear when the sentence will be carried out. Saudi Arabia has a history of carrying out executions without warning families or foreign embassies, only informing relatives after the sentence has been carried out. Anojan was prosecuted after a dispute on social media following an incident that took place during a Hindu pilgrimage in Sri Lanka. In late June, footage of a young Muslim man kicking a dog following Hindu pilgrims circulated widely on social media, triggering religious arguments online. During the exchange, a user posted derogatory remarks about a Hindu deity, leading Anojan to post a response in Tamil insulting the Prophet Muhammad. Although Anojan promptly deleted his comment and posted an apology video, it was screenshotted and brought to the attention of his employer and Saudi officials, leading to his arrest in July. His personal devices were subsequently seized, and his social media accounts were deleted by Saudi officials. “People in Saudi Arabia knew nothing about this matter. It was individuals in Sri Lanka who sent emails to the company where my brother worked. I do not even wish to mention who those people are,” Anojan’s brother, Hamsidan Sivarasa, told BBC Sinhala. The company employing Anojan notified the authorities in Saudi Arabia who registered a case against him, according to Hamsidan. Anojan was initially sentenced to five years in prison as well as a fine of 3m Saudi riyals (about $0.8m; £0.6m) by the Al-Ahsa Criminal Court. An appeal submitted on Anojan’s behalf seeking to reduce his sentence was rejected, according to Sri Lankan Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath. The case took a drastic turn on 17 September after Saudi prosecutors filed an appeal for Anojan to be prosecuted under Sharia law instead of the country’s cybercrime legislation. The appellate court granted the prosecution’s request, increasing his sentence to the death penalty. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Sri Lanka confirmed it is taking all available steps to assist Anojan. His family met President Anura Kumara Dissanayake at the Presidential Secretariat on 21 September. The president assured them that the government would spare no effort to obtain a general pardon for him, instructing diplomatic channels to engage Saudi authorities. The case has brought together cross-religious support. Senior Buddhist leaders, the Mahanayake Theros of the Ramanna Nikaya and the Amarapura Maha Nikaya, together with Hindu religious leaders, handed over a memorandum to the Presidential Secretariat calling for urgent state intervention. In addition, a four-member Sri Lankan legal delegation is travelling to Saudi Arabia this week to meet Anojan’s local defence lawyers. “There are two law firms in Saudi Arabia handling Anojan’s case. We are going there to meet the lawyers from these two firms, discuss the case and plan what can be done next,” one of the team, Upul Kumarapperuma, President’s Counsel, told BBC Sinhala. President Anura Kumara Dissanayake (fourth from right) recently met Anojan’s family Back home, communication between Anojan and his family has completely ceased. “My brother hasn’t called for two days.” Hamsidan said on 28 September. “We informed the embassy and asked officials to look into the matter and update us. They said they would check. We are still waiting, as we have not yet received a response.” In Saudi prisons, inmates on death row typically lose access to personal mobile devices, with formal calls strictly facilitated through prison authorities. Human rights organisations have repeatedly raised concerns regarding severe sentences for online speech in Saudi Arabia. In July 2023, Mohammed Al Ghamdi, a retired Saudi school teacher, was sentenced to death over his comments on multiple social media platforms, according to the United Nations. “The death sentence against Mohammad bin Nasser al-Ghamdi, who has a total of just 10 followers on both of his anonymous Twitter accounts and is accused of nothing other than expressing his opinions on social media, is ludicrous,” Philip Luther, Amnesty International’s Research and Advocacy Director for the Middle East and North Africa, said at the time. Al Ghamdi’s ruling was overturned, and he was sentenced to 30 years in prison, according to ALQST for human rights, an independent non-governmental organisation defending and promoting human rights in Saudi Arabia. There are more than 10 million foreign workers in Saudi Arabia, according to the International Organisation for Migration (IOM). Rights groups emphasise that low-wage migrant workers face distinct vulnerabilities in the Saudi legal system due to language barriers and lack of proper legal representation. Executions for blasphemy are relatively rare compared with those for drug offences or murder handed down by courts in Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Tunisie : Six Marocains expulsés, le consulat invoque des soupçons de migration clandestine
items.description: À la suite d'un article publié par Hespress au sujet des contraintes subies par des voyageurs marocains à l’aéroport international de Tunis-Carthage, le journal a reçu un nouveau témoignage de citoyens affirmant avoir été interceptés par les autorités tunisiennes puis refoulés après s’être vu refuser l’entrée sur le territoire sans aucun « motif légal ». Ils dénoncent également un traitement qu’ils qualifient d’« humiliant ». De son côté, une source au sein du consulat général du Maroc à Tunis a rejeté toute idée de traitement discriminatoire à l’égard des Marocains se rendant en Tunisie. Elle souligne que les déplacements des touristes et voyageurs marocains vers ce pays maghrébin se déroulent généralement sans difficulté et que les cas de refus d’entrée et de refoulement restent isolés. Selon cette même source, ces mesures relèvent de l’exercice d’un droit souverain des autorités tunisiennes, notamment lorsqu’existent des soupçons liés à des tentatives de migration irrégulière ou lorsque certaines informations fournies par les voyageurs suscitent des doutes quant aux véritables motifs de leur séjour. Dans la lettre adressée à Hespress , les plaignants écrivent : « Nous sommes trois jeunes Marocains âgés de 24 à 27 ans. Nous disposons tous d’un emploi stable ainsi que de revenus réguliers et confortables. Nous avions acheté des billets d’avion pour passer huit jours de vacances en Tunisie et réservé un hôtel à l’avance ». Ils poursuivent : « Nous sommes arrivés à l’aéroport Tunis-Carthage le 3 octobre 2026 à six heures du matin. À notre grande surprise, nos passeports ont été confisqués et l’entrée sur le territoire nous a été refusée. Il nous a ensuite été demandé de répondre à quelques questions générales (nom, nom du père, profession), avant d’être conduits dans une salle d’attente où l’on nous a indiqué que nous attendions une décision de l’administration ». Selon leur témoignage, ils ont alors découvert d’autres Marocains dans la même situation, dont certains voyageurs arrivés sur le même vol. « Il s’agissait notamment de commerçants et de chefs d’entreprise ayant déjà voyagé vers des destinations touristiques comme la Turquie. Nous étions au total six Marocains. Aucun motif officiel ne nous a été communiqué. Un seul agent de sécurité tunisien nous a simplement indiqué verbalement qu’il existait des soupçons selon lesquels nous envisagions une migration clandestine, sans fournir la moindre preuve. Il semble que notre âge ait contribué à alimenter ces soupçons », relatent-ils. Les voyageurs affirment également qu’aucun document attestant de leur situation professionnelle ou financière ne leur a été demandé, alors même qu’ils étaient prêts à les présenter. « Nous sommes restés retenus de six heures du matin jusqu’à 23h05 dans une salle froide, où notre demande de couper la climatisation a même été refusée. Nous avons également été contraints d’acheter un nouveau billet retour au prix de 800 dirhams afin de repartir le soir même à 23h05, alors que nous disposions déjà d’un billet de retour prévu pour le 10 octobre. Nous avons ainsi perdu ce billet ainsi que les frais d’hôtel engagés », ajoutent-ils. Les plaignants expliquent en outre qu’au moment du rapatriement, ils ont été conduits à bord de l’avion avant les autres passagers, tandis que leurs passeports étaient conservés par des agents de sécurité tunisiens. « Nous avons ressenti cela comme une humiliation, comme si nous étions des criminels », affirment-ils. Ils s’interrogent : « Si des conditions particulières s’appliquent aux Marocains souhaitant entrer en Tunisie, pourquoi ne sont-elles pas annoncées à l’avance ou pourquoi ne pas instaurer un visa ? Pourquoi laisser les voyageurs payer leurs billets et leurs réservations d’hôtel avant de les refouler après plusieurs heures de rétention ? Et pourquoi ne pas leur permettre de présenter les justificatifs nécessaires avant qu’une décision de refoulement ne soit prise, ou encore de connaître les raisons exactes du refus d’entrée ? ». Interrogée par Hespress au sujet de ces plaintes, une source du consulat général du Maroc à Tunis a affirmé que « les procédures appliquées à l’aéroport international de Tunis-Carthage sont des mesures pratiquées partout dans le monde et mises en œuvre par de nombreux États afin de protéger leurs frontières lorsqu’il existe des soupçons de migration irrégulière ». La même source précise que « les cas évoqués concernant certains voyageurs marocains refoulés à leur arrivée en Tunisie ne visent nullement la nationalité marocaine. Ils concernent des jeunes hommes constituant des cas isolés, arrivant à cette période particulière de l’année, connue pour correspondre au pic de la migration irrégulière en Tunisie. Cette situation suscite des interrogations de la part des autorités aéroportuaires, qui peuvent alors décider de leur refoulement ». Le responsable ajoute que certains voyageurs alimentent eux-mêmes ces soupçons en fournissant « des informations peu crédibles » sur leurs lieux de séjour. Selon lui, certains présentent des réservations dans des localités, villages ou régions réputés pour être des points de départ de réseaux de passeurs et qui ne disposent ni d’infrastructures touristiques ni de plages attractives. Ces doutes sont renforcés lorsque les passagers voyagent avec des bagages légers ne correspondant pas à un séjour touristique classique. La source de Hespress insiste par ailleurs sur le fait que « le passage des Marocains dans les aéroports tunisiens s’effectue dans des conditions parfaitement normales. Des Marocains et des Marocaines entrent quotidiennement en Tunisie sans rencontrer le moindre obstacle ». Elle estime que les accusations d’un traitement sélectif à l’égard des voyageurs marocains sont « dénuées de fondement » et qu’elles relèvent d’une polémique entretenue par « certains jeunes dont la tentative de rejoindre l’Europe via la Tunisie n’aurait peut-être pas abouti et qui ont été refoulés dans le cadre de l’exercice du droit souverain des autorités tunisiennes ». Enfin, la source consulaire conclut en soulignant que « ce type d’allégations et de plaintes revient chaque année à la même période, lorsque la migration irrégulière atteint son pic en Tunisie ». Elle relève également que certaines informations fournies aux autorités tunisiennes par de jeunes voyageurs marocains paraissent peu cohérentes, citant notamment le cas de personnes affirmant venir pratiquer le tourisme balnéaire dans des régions où les températures sont déjà fraîches, alors même que les Tunisiens eux-mêmes désertent ces zones à cette période de l’année. The post Tunisie : Six Marocains expulsés, le consulat invoque des soupçons de migration clandestine appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Pakistan opposes new permanent Security Council members
items.description: • Asim Iftikhar says Islamabad backs more elected seats on UNSC • Foreign secretary-designate highlights country’s role in peaceful dispute settlement • Notes Islamabad presses for peaceful settlement of Kashmir dispute WASHINGTON: Pakistan opposes adding new permanent members to the UN Security Council and instead favours increasing the number of elected, non-permanent members of the 15-member body, Pakistan’s UN envoy Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad, who is set to take charge as the country’s new foreign secretary next week, told Dawn. Assessing Pakistan’s stint on the Security Council, from 2025 to 2026, he discussed the major international crises and diplomatic initiatives that marked his tenure. Mr Ahmad is returning to Islamabad after serving as Pakistan’s permanent representative to the UN and will take charge as the new foreign secretary. “Developments in recent years in the peace and security landscape and within the Security Council, as well as increased criticism of the role of the permanent members, have further reinforced the belief of a wide majority of member states that we need a more democratic, representative and accountable Security Council,” he said. “Adding any new individual permanent members would only aggravate the problem. In simple words, the problem cannot be the solution.” Pakistan, he said, had advocated, along with members of the Uniting for Consensus group and other like-minded countries, a reformed Council with more elected members, including medium-term seats based on periodic elections and rotation. “Pakistan and many other countries are eminently qualified to bring their contribution to the Security Council and the maintenance of international peace and security,” Mr Ahmad said. “Member states should be ready to fulfil that responsibility without permanence and privilege.” Pakistan’s 2025-26 term was its eighth tenure on the Security Council. For Mr Ahmad personally, it was his third consecutive Council assignment, having previously served on Pakistan’s teams in 2003-04 and 2012-13. “It is such a great and singular honour to have the opportunity to represent Pakistan at the United Nations including at the Security Council,” he said. He said Pakistan entered its latest Council term with considerable diplomatic and institutional experience and had identified conflict prevention and peaceful settlement of disputes, peacekeeping, counterterrorism and cooperation with regional organisations as key priorities. “We were able to achieve a lot in all of those domains,” he said. The term, however, unfolded against a backdrop of deep geopolitical tensions, including a sharp deterioration in relations between India and Pakistan that culminated in a four-day military confrontation in May 2025 , bringing the two nuclear-armed neighbours dangerously close to a wider conflict. Mr Ahmad said the crisis also reinforced Pakistan’s emphasis on peaceful settlement of disputes and highlighted the importance of diplomacy in preventing conflicts from escalating. He pointed to Security Council Resolution 2788, adopted unanimously during Pakistan’s presidency of the Council in July 2025, as one of the major achievements of the country’s term. The Pakistan-sponsored resolution placed renewed emphasis on the mechanisms provided by the UN Charter for the peaceful settlement of international disputes. Despite what Mr Ahmad described as a “polarised Council”, Pakistan was able to forge consensus around the resolution. “This landmark resolution has been the most widely referred Council decision ever since its adoption, something that testifies to its importance and relevance to Council’s work,” he said. “It is also worth recalling that Pakistan initiated and steered this resolution that lays emphasis on peaceful resolution of disputes, having inflicted a crushing defeat to the Indian aggression in May 2025,” he said. Mr Ahmad also highlighted what he described as Pakistan’s practical contribution to peaceful dispute settlement beyond the Security Council. He said Pakistan had played an important role in mediating between the United States and Iran, helping bring about a ceasefire in April, facilitating the Islamabad talks and contributing to the process that led to the signing of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding in June. “Our leadership remains closely engaged with all sides and other friends and partners to advance the prospects of peace,” he said. On Palestine, Mr Ahmad said Pakistan had remained a “forceful voice” in the Council and played a key role in supporting the Comprehensive Plan on Gaza and Security Council Resolution 2803. The measures, he said, helped bring about a ceasefire, opened humanitarian space in Gaza and, importantly, restored a political horizon for Palestinian self-determination and statehood. Pakistan also used several Arria Formula meetings of the Security Council to focus attention on the unresolved Jammu and Kashmir dispute and the need for its peaceful settlement in accordance with international legitimacy and relevant Security Council resolutions. Published in Dawn, October 6th, 2026

items.title: US warns foreign financial institutions not to do business with Iran
items.description: The United States on Monday warned foreign financial institutions that if they conducted any business with Iran or its banking sector they could be sanctioned by Washington. “Foreign financial institutions continuing to transact with sanctioned Iranian financial institutions could be targeted at any time without advance notification and should take immediate action to terminate such activity and relationships,” the US Treasury said in an “alert” statement. The United States launched its war against Iran in late February, killing the country’s leadership and demanding it cease any nuclear-related activities. The war has plunged the Middle East into violence, with Tehran’s retaliatory action targeting Washington’s Gulf allies and sending global energy and fertilizer prices skyrocketing after it virtually shut a key trading route. Since late August, Washington has stepped up its campaign to economically isolate Tehran, warning its allies that they would be hit by secondary sanctions if they continued to conduct transactions with the country’s government. The US Treasury has also announced a slew of new sanctions as part of that push, targeting Iran’s financial, cryptocurrency, rail, automotive and manufacturing sectors. It has also taken action against two banks — one in the United Arab Emirates and another in Turkey — over their alleged aid to the authorities in Tehran. In Monday’s statement, the Treasury said Iran’s government operated so-called “shadow banking” channels to circumvent US sanctions, and that foreign financial institutions should aim to identify and avoid any such activities. AFP The post US warns foreign financial institutions not to do business with Iran appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NPP to deliberately select candidates for orphan constituencies ahead of 2028 election
items.description: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) is planning a more deliberate approach to selecting parliamentary candidates in constituencies where it has no sitting Member of Parliament ahead of the 2028 elections. Newly elected Third Vice Chairperson of the party, Nana Akomea, says the strategy will involve assessing the demographics of these “orphan constituencies” before candidates are selected. He said the approach is not entirely new but will be implemented on a larger and more deliberate scale. “No, but it’s not new. Every party does that.” Nana Akomea said the NPP now has more constituencies without sitting MPs and enough time to plan its parliamentary strategy carefully. “But what is essential is the demography. We have a bit of time now to look at the demography of each of the orphan constituencies.” He said constituency parties will be expected to provide information on the demographics of their areas. “The constituency party will bring us reports about the demography, and they would suggest that for this constituency, if we get a candidate from this demography, it will help us.” According to him, taking such decisions early will prevent prospective candidates from investing heavily in campaigns only to be rejected later. “When that determination is made early, then somebody who is not from that demography will not go and waste time and money to campaign, and then later on you decide that, oh, he may not win.” He said such candidates could already have built support and become emotionally invested in the contest by the time the party reaches a different conclusion. “But then he’s already invested money. He’s already got followers. His emotions involved.” Nana Akomea said the NPP had used a similar approach ahead of the 2000 elections. “Look, in the NPP going to the 2000 elections, we did the same exercise.” He cited the profiling of constituencies in Accra’s coastal areas as an example. “We had a lot of constituencies with no sitting MPs, and we decided that the coastal area of Accra, for example, should be reserved for Gas. That is profiling, and so on.” He also defended the party’s decision to identify potential candidates who are not currently members of the NPP. “Every party does that.” Nana Akomea said the difference ahead of 2028 will be the scale and the level of planning. “So it is not new. Is that we’re going to do it on a scale that is more deliberate, and that is more fulfilling.” He said the NPP’s early internal reorganisation has also given the party more time to prepare for the next general election. “We have a bit of time.” He linked the early selection of the party’s flagbearer to the reduced tension during the recent national executive elections. “We secured for ourselves the blessing of time by doing this reorganisation, selecting the flagbearer 2-3 years ahead of the elections, and you would see the wisdom in that action has cascaded.” Nana Akomea said the party’s immediate task is now to get its parliamentary strategy right. “What we need to do now is to get the parliamentary thing right.”

items.title: Moscow moot ends sans joint statement
items.description: • Pakistan-Afghanistan disagreement cited as main reason • Islamabad maintains cross-border terror attacks rose despite peace talks with Taliban • ICC unseals warrants for Afghan ministers over anti-women actions ISLAMABAD: The eighth edition of the Moscow Format regional consultations on Afghanistan on Monday ended without a joint communique, mainly because of disagreements between Pakistani and Afghan delegations in what was possibly the first instance in the series where participants failed to agree on a joint statement. Russian presidential envoy for Afghanistan Zamir Kabulov said Moscow regretted that the participants could not agree on the final document. “When drafting the final joint statement, we encountered one problem, that problem was that our Afghan and Pakistani colleagues didn’t see eye to eye,” he said. The Moscow meeting brought together special envoys and senior officials from Afghanistan, China, India, Iran, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Russia, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan, with Belarus and Egypt attending as guests. The format dates back to 2016 -17 and has emerged as one of the main regional diplomatic tracks on Afghanistan. The failure to agree on a joint statement underscored how the worsening Pakistan-Afghanistan dispute is now complicating wider regional efforts to build consensus on Afghanistan. The tense relations between Islamabad and Kabul were among the key issues discussed at the meeting, with the dispute over terrorism and counterterrorism language ultimately preventing the adoption of the joint document. Mr Kabulov said the Afghan side objected to references that placed Afghanistan in a terrorist context. Attacks from Afghan soil Pakistan’s special envoy for Afghanistan, Moha­mmad Sadiq, told the meeting that Islamabad wanted peace and stability in the region and had pursued political and diplomatic engagement with the Taliban leadership to address terrorism emanating from Afghan soil. “Pakistan desires peace and stability in the region and has remained patiently engaged in political and diplomatic efforts aimed at addressing the menace of terrorism emanating from Afghan soil. However, it is unfortunate that Pakistan’s numerous goodwill gestures and highly responsible appr­oach were misconstrued, resulting in increased terrorist attacks from Afghan soil, with the active support and backing of the Taliban Regime,” he said. Taliban want more talks Afghan Taliban Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi, meanwhile, criticised Pakistan’s statements and actions towards Afghanistan and Afghans, accusing Islamabad of using military pressure, refugees, students and transit routes as instruments of leverage. At the same time, he insisted that the problems affecting relations bet­ween the two neighbours could be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy. Russia offered to help de-escalate the dispute, although Kabulov stressed that resolving bilateral disputes was not the purpose of the Moscow Format. “Russia is ready to assist in ending this conflict in any possible, permissible way either on its own or in partnership with our other partners provided that both sides make such a request. We are ready to provide the maximum possible assistance,” he said. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, who opened the meeting, endorsed the performance of the Taliban authorities while warning against any attempt by Nato to establish military infrastructure in Afghanistan or neighbouring countries. He backed assistance to Kabul and said strengthening Afghanistan’s counterterrorism capacity served regional interests. ICC warrants Meanwhile, the Inter­national Criminal Court on Monday unsealed arrest warrants for two Afghan ministers accused of committing crimes against humanity through the Taliban government’s restrictions on women and girls, AFP reported. The warrants, for Habibullah Agha, minister of education, and Neda Mohammad Nadeem, minister of higher education, were issued in September 2025 but remained under seal until Monday. The two officials are accused of gender-based persecution linked to policies that have barred girls from attending school beyond primary level and excluded women from higher education following the Taliban’s return to power in August 2021. The two warrants against the ministers were issued after the ICC, in July 2025, authorised warrants for Afghanistan’s Supreme Taliban Leader Haibatullah Akhundzada and Supreme Court President Abdul Hakim Haqqani, parts of which have been made public. Both Agha and Nadeem were instrumental in imposing the supreme leader’s vision of Afghanistan. In a sharp reaction to the ICC warrants, a Taliban spokesman condemned the ICC position on the arrest of Afghan leaders. Published in Dawn, October 6th, 2026

items.title: Beyond diversification of ports
items.description: The Federal Government’s approval for the comprehensive modernisation of Onne, Delta and Calabar ports, alongside establishment of six new deep seaports, is laudable. It is a potentially transformative attempt to dismantle the excessive concentration of Nigeria’s maritime commerce around Lagos. The approved projects are Ibom, Bakassi, Agge, Gateway, Ondo and Bonny, building on the modernisation of Apapa and Tin Can Island ports. For years, maritime stakeholders have complained that Lagos bears a disproportionate share of national cargo, imposing congestion, delays and additional logistics costs on importers, exporters, manufacturers, transporters and consumers. The Nigerian Shippers’ Council recently acknowledged that the under-utilisation of Eastern ports increases logistics costs and limits supply-chain efficiency. A recent maritime editors’ conference also described the imbalance between Lagos and Eastern ports as economically unhealthy and unsustainable. If implemented faithfully, the new policy could give all eight littoral states—Lagos, Ogun, Ondo, Delta, Bayelsa, Rivers, Akwa Ibom and Cross River—functional port gateways. That geographical spread matters. It can bring cargo closer to producers and consumers, shorten inland haulage distances, reduce pressure on Lagos, stimulate competition among ports, attract shipping lines, create jobs, encourage industrial clusters and expand government revenue. It can also strengthen agricultural and mineral exports, support manufacturing, stimulate warehousing and logistics, and open new corridors to neighbouring countries. There is a deeper national-unity dividend. Ports distributed across the federation can make economic opportunity less geographically concentrated. Businesses in the South-East, South-South, North-Central and far North need not depend disproportionately on Lagos for international trade. Such connectivity can deepen economic interdependence among regions and give communities a stronger stake in the federation. But the policy should not stop at the coastline. The Federal Government should expand its vision to inland ports linked efficiently to seaports by rail, road and waterways. The proposed Azumini Port in Abia, the Onitsha Port in Anambra, and viable inland gateways around Lokoja, Makurdi and Baro deserve immediate approval. The more strategically connected ports Nigeria develops, the more widely the benefits of maritime commerce can circulate. The connectivity vision articulated by the Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, is therefore welcome. We must actualise berths, dredged channels, cargo equipment, rail lines, roads, digital customs systems and reliable operations. Nigeria has witnessed too many port promises stranded between approval and execution. This is also where scepticism about President Bola Tinubu’s Lagos connections must be answered—not with rhetoric, but with results. Lagos should remain a major maritime gateway, but it should no longer carry an unhealthy concentration of national cargo simply because alternatives are neglected. The Federal Government must now finance, coordinate and execute the diversification decisively, in partnership with the states and the private sector. If it does, the country will gain a genuinely connected national economy and a more balanced federation. That is the productive diversification we need. The post Beyond diversification of ports appeared first on Vanguard News .
